clue.text: Tell uncle perhaps after four quit

indicators.note: to quit is to leave, so the Roman four walks out of the relative

parts.note: an uncle is one example of a relative
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A storyteller is urged to tell a tale about an uncle once four people have left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after four quit' reads as time passing; the uncle is just one kind of relative, and the four is a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to narrate it, a straightforward synonym of tell.

clue.text: Reserved this occasionally in 4

explanation.surface: Something kept back, appearing now and then in a cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: The '4' points to the answer of 4-across, UP-TO-DATE, whose synonym RECENT holds the alternate letters T and I of 'this'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reticent person is reserved, keeping thoughts and feelings to themselves.

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Before shaving you work up a foam of soap on the face, so lathering is preparation for it.

explanation.definitionFit: A tiepin holds a necktie securely in place, a small fastening device.

clue.text: Trendy university head traps fox

explanation.definitionFit: Up-to-date means current or modern, a near synonym of fashionable.

clue.text: One shows film boss going up first after cast

parts.note: to cast an image is to project it

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

first is written 1ST, with the figure read as I

explanation.surface: A film boss takes priority once the cast is chosen.
explanation.walkthrough: Digits stand in as letters: boss is NO. 1, reading NOI, and 'going up' turns it into ION; first is 1ST, giving IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A projectionist is the person who runs the projector that screens a film in a cinema.

clue.text: Leg exercises broach average in theory

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side, so leg gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true on paper holds in principle or theory, though perhaps not in practice.

clue.text: Group of Arab horses can't stand

explanation.definitionFit: To abhor is to loathe, which is to find something unbearable.

clue.text: Assuming power, try hard to acquire boffin

explanation.walkthrough: 'Assuming power' says the same thing as 'to acquire': the P is taken inside EXERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Boffin is British slang for a scientific expert or specialist.

clue.text: Young winger is rashly replaced after cold

clue.text: Liberal, say, upset and edgy, ignoring victor
